        - name: "Related Datasets with Typed Relationships"

      scoring_method: "Sum of sub_element presence / 5"

18	description: >-
19	  CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access critical care dataset
20	  produced by the Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for
21	  Equitable AI project, one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium.
22	  Data are collected retrospectively from the clinical systems of 14 data contributing hospitals
23	  within a collaboration spanning 20 academic centers, and are harmonized to unified standards:
24	  structured electronic health record data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, imaging
25	  from PACS is held as DICOM, bedside monitor telemetry as WFDB waveforms, hospital EEG as EDF+ and
26	  Persyst, and clinical notes are extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit. The current
27	  released dataset reported by the project website comprises 50,000 patient admissions from ICU,
28	  PICU and NICU settings, 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data,
29	  and 23 Tb of waveform data; the anticipated final dataset covers 100,000 patient admissions across
30	  9 data modalities. All data types are under controlled access. As presented in September 2025,
31	  OMOP and telemetry data reside in a cloud enclave, clinical notes are stored locally at the
32	  contributing sites except for tokens, imaging de-identification was in process for a larger cohort,
33	  and EEG extraction was in process. Data acquisition, standardization and modality expansion
34	  continue within the NIH project period 2022-09-01 through 2026-11-30.

# D4D Datasheet for CHORUS Dataset
# Generation Method: schema-grounded agentic, phase 1
# Agent runtime: Claude API (direct)
# Provider: LBL CBORG (proxy to Anthropic)
# Model: claude-opus-5
# Mode: four-phase project agent, generic-v8 prompt
# Prompt: src/download/prompts/d4d_generic_arm_prompt_v8.md (identical for all projects)
# Arm: BASELINE (input documents only)
# Source bundle: data/preprocessed/concatenated/CHORUS_preprocessed.txt
# Source manifest: data/preprocessed/source_manifest.yaml
# Schema: src/data_sheets_schema/schema/data_sheets_schema_all.yaml
# Prior D4D factual reuse: prohibited
# Temperature: 0.0

id: https://chorus4ai.org/
name: CHoRUS Dataset
title: "Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI"
description: >-
  CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access critical care dataset
  produced by the Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for
  Equitable AI project, one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium.
  Data are collected retrospectively from the clinical systems of 14 data contributing hospitals
  within a collaboration spanning 20 academic centers, and are harmonized to unified standards:
  structured electronic health record data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, imaging
  from PACS is held as DICOM, bedside monitor telemetry as WFDB waveforms, hospital EEG as EDF+ and
  Persyst, and clinical notes are extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit. The current
  released dataset reported by the project website comprises 50,000 patient admissions from ICU,
  PICU and NICU settings, 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data,
  and 23 Tb of waveform data; the anticipated final dataset covers 100,000 patient admissions across
  9 data modalities. All data types are under controlled access. As presented in September 2025,
  OMOP and telemetry data reside in a cloud enclave, clinical notes are stored locally at the
  contributing sites except for tokens, imaging de-identification was in process for a larger cohort,
  and EEG extraction was in process. Data acquisition, standardization and modality expansion
  continue within the NIH project period 2022-09-01 through 2026-11-30.
keywords:
  - critical care
  - intensive care unit
  - acute illness
  - electronic health record
  - OMOP Common Data Model
  - waveform telemetry
  - electroencephalography
  - medical imaging
  - clinical notes
  - social determinants of health
  - AI-ready dataset
  - Bridge2AI
  - multimodal data
  - controlled access
status: released
page: https://chorus4ai.org/
source_caveats: >-
  The two mid-tier sources report different admission totals for the released data: the project
  website (project_documentation, higher ranked) states a Current Released Dataset of 50,000 patient
  admissions, while the September 2025 AIM-AHEAD informational webinar (cohort_2_webinar) states
  that "As of August 2025" the dataset "covers 14 different hospitals with over 45K unique
  admissions"; the higher-ranked website figure is used here and the webinar figure is recorded in
  this caveat. Imaging volume is likewise reported two ways and on different units: the website
  reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data, the webinar reports 1000 images currently available
  with de-identification in process for a larger cohort. Anticipated final figures (100,000
  admissions, 9 modalities) are stated by the website as anticipated, not released. The webinar's
  data-type table has a Metadata column containing both "Yes" and "Planned" values and a separate
  column naming per-modality metadata schemas, but the table's text is interleaved in the bundle in
  a way that does not permit reliable assignment of those column values to individual data types, so
  neither per-modality metadata status nor per-modality metadata schema is asserted here; only the
  table's unambiguous Data standard column is used. The project website carries a site-wide banner
  reading "This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with
  Administration directives" (spelling as published). The chorus-ai GitHub overview was captured
  2025-11-14 and is the lowest-ranked source in the bundle.
conforms_to: >-
  OMOP Common Data Model for structured EHR data (demographics, medication administration,
  procedures, diagnoses and nursing flowsheets); DICOM for imaging; WFDB for waveform telemetry;
  EDF+ and Persyst for waveform EEG; OHNLP for extracted and tokenized clinical notes.

  archives, bedside monitor gateway/middleware, and hospital EEG databases of 14 contributing
  hospitals.

purposes:
  - response: >-
      To develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring the methods
      promote privacy, accountability and clinical benefit, and while promoting a new generation of
      AI clinicians and scientists.
  - response: >-
      To develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set to answer
      the grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.
  - response: >-
      To create ethically sourced datasets and tools around artificial intelligence and to create
      best practices for AI in health, in collaboration with the other Bridge2AI data generation
      projects.
  - response: >-
      To develop capabilities across a multi-center network to acquire, standardize, tokenize,
      store, visualize and label structured EHR data, tokenized unstructured EHR data, telemetry and
      EEG waveforms, imaging, and social determinants of health.
  - response: >-
      To ensure that data elements feature appropriate contextual factors such as geographic
      distance to the nearest hospital.
tasks:
  - response: Characterizing acute and critical care illness.
  - response: Predicting complications among patients with acute or critical illness.
  - response: Measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.
  - response: >-
      External validation of AI/ML models against a sequestered holdout dataset, to aid marketplace
      adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.
addressing_gaps:
  - response: >-
      There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine
      learning in critical care; developing high-resolution multi-center data sets is a critical
      first step towards actionable and trustworthy AI.
  - response: >-
      Existing resources lack a diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready dataset for
      the grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.
  - response: >-
      Absence of sequestered holdout data for external validation of models developed on critical
      care data, which the project addresses by sequestering holdout datasets.
  - response: >-
      Lack of unified standards across multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging and text data, which the
      project addresses through harmonization and validated semantic mappings.
acquisition_methods:
  - acquisition_details: >-
      Retrospective data collection: data documented during routine clinical care are extracted from
      the source systems of contributing hospitals (EHR, PACS, bedside monitors and gateway or
      middleware, and the hospital EEG database) and delivered as site data extracts.
    was_directly_observed: true
  - acquisition_details: >-
      Derived content: unstructured EHR text is extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit, and
      OMOP Location entities are geocoded with open source code via DeGauss.
    was_inferred_derived: true
collection_mechanisms:
  - mechanism_details: >-
      Bedside monitors with gateway/middleware capture for waveform telemetry, converted with the
      CHoRUS waveform conversion scripts maintained in the chorus_waveform repository.
  - mechanism_details: >-
      The OHNLP toolkit, used to extract and tokenize clinical notes at contributing sites.
  - mechanism_details: >-
      Site data extracts created and uploaded using the chorus-extract-upload tooling, following
      standard operating protocols published on the centralized Chorus_SOP documentation site.
collection_timeframes:
  - timeframe_details: >-
      Retrospective collection of previously recorded clinical data at contributing hospitals; as
      presented in September 2025, the assembled dataset reflected a state as of August 2025, with
      further acquisition continuing within the project period.

    collector_details: >-
      14 data contributing hospitals supply clinical data extracts; the collaboration spans 20
      academic centers, of which 14 contribute as Data Acquisition centers.
  - name: Site data managers at contributing sites
    role: data site manager
    collector_details: >-
      Data managers at contributing sites follow the interactive Chorus_SOP workflow to extract and
      contribute clinical data, and provide regular status updates on their extract progress through
      GitHub or a Google Form that updates the Standards and Data Acquisition project boards.
direct_collection:
  - is_direct: false
    collection_details: >-
      Data are not collected from individuals for the purpose of this dataset; they are
      retrospectively extracted from clinical source systems at contributing hospitals and delivered
      to the CHoRUS environment as site data extracts.
sampling_strategies:
  - is_sample: true
    strategies: >-
      Sampling to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies;
      federated access is intended to enable sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse
      cohort across the contributing centers.
    source_caveats: >-
      The bundle states the sampling intent but does not describe the executed sampling frame,
      inclusion criteria, or any verification of representativeness.
raw_data_sources:
  - source_description: Structured electronic health record data from contributing hospitals.
    source_type: hospital electronic health record system
    raw_data_format: >-
      Source EHR formats, transformed to the OMOP Common Data Model (demographics, medication
      administration with dosing time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration,
      procedures documented by providers, diagnoses documented by providers, and high-frequency
      nursing flowsheet documentation).
    access_details: Controlled access.
  - source_description: Unstructured clinical notes from the electronic health record.
    source_type: hospital electronic health record system
    raw_data_format: Free text, extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit.
    access_details: >-
      Controlled access; clinical notes are stored locally at the contributing sites, with only
      tokens held centrally.
  - source_description: Radiology imaging drawn from hospital PACS archives.
    source_type: picture archiving and communication system
    raw_data_format: DICOM.
    access_details: Controlled access.
  - source_description: Continuous physiologic waveform telemetry from bedside monitors.
    source_type: bedside monitor with gateway/middleware capture
    raw_data_format: WFDB.
    access_details: Controlled access; held in the cloud enclave.
  - source_description: Electroencephalography recordings from the hospital EEG database.
    source_type: hospital EEG database
    raw_data_format: EDF+ and Persyst.
    access_details: >-
      Controlled access; extraction was in process at the time of the September 2025 webinar.
preprocessing_strategies:
  - preprocessing_details: >-
      Standardization of source clinical data to the OMOP Common Data Model, supported by validated
      semantic mappings for connecting clinical data in various source formats to international
      standards; pooled tabular mappings and an associated clinical validation SOP are maintained in
      the chorus-mapping repository.
  - preprocessing_details: >-
      Extraction and tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text using the OHNLP
      toolkit, so that only tokens leave the contributing site.
  - preprocessing_details: >-
      Transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification; imaging
      de-identification was in process for the larger cohort as of September 2025.
  - preprocessing_details: >-
      Waveform conversion using the documentation and conversion scripts maintained in the
      chorus_waveform repository, with additional resources supporting the preparation and release of
      waveforms.
  - preprocessing_details: >-
      Geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss, using open source code maintained in the
      UF-Geocoding repository.
cleaning_strategies:
  - cleaning_details: >-
      Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data
      submissions, allowing sites to identify and resolve issues in their extracts.
  - cleaning_details: >-
      Standard operating protocols instruct data contributing sites on best practices for curating
      and delivering interoperable datasets; SOP documents undergo an internal validation and review
      process before publication.
instances:
  - instance_type: Patient admission from an ICU, PICU or NICU setting.
    counts: 50000
    data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:4
    description: >-
      Admissions in the current released dataset as reported by the project website; the anticipated
      final dataset covers 100,000 patient admissions.
  - instance_type: Row of OMOP-standardized electronic health record data.
    counts: 1600000000
    data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37
    data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:9
    description: >-
      Rows of EHR OMOP data in the current released dataset. The project website states the figure
      as "1.6 Billion"; the integer recorded here is that approximate magnitude expanded to units.
  - instance_type: Admission accompanied by radiology imaging data.
    counts: 7642
    data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11
    data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:15
    description: >-
      Admissions with radiology data in the current released dataset per the project website; the
      September 2025 webinar reported 1000 images currently available with de-identification in
      process for a larger cohort.
  - instance_type: Bedside monitor waveform telemetry recording.
    data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:49
    data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:37
    description: 23 Tb of waveform data in the current released dataset.
subsets:
  - id: https://chorus4ai.org/#subset-demographics
    name: Demographics
    description: Patient demographic data held under controlled access.
    conforms_to: OMOP Common Data Model
    conforms_to_standard:
      - OMOP_CDM
    is_data_split: false
    is_subpopulation: false
  - id: https://chorus4ai.org/#subset-medication-administration
    name: Medication administration
    description: >-
      Medication administration records with dosing time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose
      administration, held under controlled access.
    conforms_to: OMOP Common Data Model
    conforms_to_standard:
      - OMOP_CDM
    is_data_split: false
    is_subpopulation: false
  - id: https://chorus4ai.org/#subset-procedures
    name: Procedures
    description: Procedures as documented by providers, held under controlled access.
    conforms_to: OMOP Common Data Model
    conforms_to_standard:
      - OMOP_CDM
    is_data_split: false
    is_subpopulation: false
  - id: https://chorus4ai.org/#subset-nursing-flowsheets
    name: Nursing flowsheets
    description: High-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation, held under controlled access.
    conforms_to: OMOP Common Data Model
    conforms_to_standard:
      - OMOP_CDM
    is_data_split: false
    is_subpopulation: false
  - id: https://chorus4ai.org/#subset-diagnoses
    name: Diagnoses
    description: Diagnoses as documented by providers, held under controlled access.
    conforms_to: OMOP Common Data Model
    conforms_to_standard:
      - OMOP_CDM
    is_data_split: false
    is_subpopulation: false
  - id: https://chorus4ai.org/#subset-clinical-notes
    name: Clinical notes
    description: >-
      Clinical notes extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit, held under controlled access;
      the notes themselves are stored locally at the contributing sites, with only tokens held
      centrally.
    conforms_to: OHNLP
    conforms_to_standard:
      - OTHER
    is_data_split: false
    is_subpopulation: false
  - id: https://chorus4ai.org/#subset-imaging
    name: Imaging
    description: >-
      Imaging drawn from hospital PACS, held under controlled access. As of the September 2025
      webinar, 1000 images were available and de-identification was in process for a larger cohort;
      the project website reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data in the current released
      dataset.
    conforms_to: DICOM
    conforms_to_standard:
      - DICOM
    is_data_split: false
    is_subpopulation: false
  - id: https://chorus4ai.org/#subset-waveform-telemetry
    name: Waveform telemetry
    description: >-
      Waveform telemetry captured from bedside monitors via gateway/middleware, held in the enclave
      under controlled access; the current released dataset includes 23 Tb of waveform data.
    conforms_to: WFDB
    conforms_to_standard:
      - WFDB
    is_data_split: false
    is_subpopulation: false
  - id: https://chorus4ai.org/#subset-waveform-eeg
    name: Waveform EEG
    description: >-
      Electroencephalography waveforms drawn from the hospital EEG database, held under controlled
      access; extraction was in process at the time of the September 2025 webinar.
    conforms_to: EDF+ and Persyst
    conforms_to_standard:
      - OTHER
    is_data_split: false
    is_subpopulation: false
subpopulations:
  - subpopulation_elements_present: true
    identification: >-
      Adult intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, identified by the care setting of the admission.
  - subpopulation_elements_present: true
    identification: >-
      Pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions, identified by the care setting of the
      admission.
  - subpopulation_elements_present: true
    identification: >-
      Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions, identified by the care setting of the
      admission.
splits:
  - split_details: >-
      The project states that the dataset will also provision a holdout test set, accessible for
      model external validation to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models; sequestering
      holdout datasets for external validation is described as a planned project activity rather
      than a released partition.
known_limitations:
  - limitation_type: coverage_limitation
    limitation_description: >-
      Imaging coverage is partial: as of the September 2025 webinar only 1000 images were available,
      with de-identification in process for a larger cohort.
  - limitation_type: coverage_limitation
    limitation_description: >-
      EEG waveform data were still being extracted at the time of the September 2025 webinar and
      were therefore not fully available to users.
  - limitation_type: integration_limitation
    limitation_description: >-
      Clinical note text is stored locally at the contributing sites rather than in the enclave;
      only tokens are centrally available, which constrains analyses requiring full note text.
  - limitation_type: scope_limitation
    limitation_description: >-
      The dataset covers acute and critical care admissions (ICU, PICU and NICU) contributed by 14
      hospitals, so it does not represent care outside these settings or these institutions.
  - limitation_type: coverage_limitation
    limitation_description: >-
      The released dataset of 50,000 admissions is smaller than the anticipated final dataset of
      100,000 admissions across 9 data modalities.
known_biases:
  - bias_type: selection_bias
    bias_description: >-
      The cohort is assembled from 14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration of 20
      academic centers, so patient case mix reflects the populations served by those centers.
    mitigation_strategy: >-
      Federated access is intended to enable sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse
      cohort; the project additionally samples to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions
      and clinical treatment strategies, and patient-focused efforts determine ethical and legal
      approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health.
    source_caveats: >-
      The bundle documents the project's bias-management intent and the composition of the
      contributing network; it does not report a measured bias assessment for the released data.
sensitive_elements:
  - sensitive_elements_present: true
    sensitivity_details: >-
      The dataset consists of clinical data about critically ill patients, including diagnoses,
      procedures, medication administration, nursing flowsheets, clinical notes, imaging, telemetry
      and EEG waveforms, and social determinants of health with geographic context such as distance
      to the nearest hospital.
confidential_elements:
  - confidential_elements_present: true
    confidentiality_details: >-
      Every data type is listed with controlled access. OMOP and telemetry data sit in the enclave;
      clinical notes are not placed in the enclave but stored locally at contributing sites, with
      only tokens shared.
is_deidentified:
  identifiable_elements_present: true
  method: >-
    Extraction and tokenization of unstructured EHR text with the OHNLP toolkit; de-identification
    of imaging, in process for the larger cohort as of September 2025; transformation of data using
    approaches that limit re-identification.
  deidentification_details: >-
    De-identification is combined with controlled access rather than relied on alone: users are
    granted access to a provisioned environment after registration and a signed licensing agreement.
    Identifiable source material remains at the contributing sites, where clinical note text is
    stored locally and only tokens are shared.
participant_privacy:
  - anonymization_method: >-
      Tokenization of clinical note text, imaging de-identification, and transformations designed to
      limit re-identification.
    privacy_techniques: >-
      A privacy scan tool for medical records is maintained by the project, alongside controlled
      access to all data types.
    reidentification_risk: >-
      The project describes transforming data using approaches that limit re-identification, and
      patient-focused efforts to determine ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy.
human_subject_research:
  involves_human_subjects: true
  special_populations:
  - >-
    Includes pediatric (PICU) and neonatal (NICU) intensive care admissions as well as adult
    critically ill patients.
  notes: >-
    The dataset is assembled retrospectively from the clinical records of critically ill patients,
    with a target of more than 100,000 critically ill patients across the project.
at_risk_populations:
  at_risk_groups_included: true
  special_protections:
  - >-
    All data types are under controlled access; clinical notes remain at the contributing sites
    except for tokens, and data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification.
  notes: >-
    Pediatric and neonatal intensive care admissions are within scope, and the population consists
    of acutely and critically ill patients.
ethical_reviews:
  - review_details: >-
      The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is
      appropriate for public sharing, and evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI to
      find ways to increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in AI.
    source_caveats: >-
      The bundle documents these ethics activities as project workstreams (the CHoRUS Ethics pillar,
      "Ethical and Trustworthy AI"); it names no institutional review board, ethics committee or
      compliance certification, and no reviewing organization is asserted here.
data_governance:
  accountable_organization:
    name: Massachusetts General Hospital
    description: >-
      Awardee organization for NIH award OT2OD032701 and home institution of the project's principal
      investigator.
  committee_contact:
    id: https://chorus4ai.org/#person-jared-houghtaling
    name: Jared Houghtaling
    email: jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org
  access_review_process: >-
    Access is controlled for all data types. Access requests are directed to the contacts published
    in the chorus-ai GitHub README: dbold@emory.edu or jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org. Under the
    AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program, participants complete a registration form
    giving name, email and institution, and receive an email once access is granted and compute has
    been provisioned.
  source_caveats: >-
    The chorus-ai GitHub README lists two co-equal access-request addresses, dbold@emory.edu and
    jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org. Only one can be carried in the single-valued
    committee_contact; the other is recorded in access_review_process, so the two contacts are
    represented asymmetrically. The README gives no name, role or organization for either address
    beyond the address itself; no affiliation is asserted for the structured contact.
license_and_use_terms:
  license_terms: >-
    Controlled access to all data types. Participants must sign a licensing agreement, included in
    the registration form, before gaining access to the dataset; under the training program route a
    ".edu" email address is required to gain access to the dataset, and program administrators will
    assist with this access if needed.
  source_caveats: >-
    The chorus-ai GitHub README states that "This project is licensed under the MIT License", which
    is recorded here as applying to the project's software repositories rather than to the clinical
    dataset, whose access is governed by the signed licensing agreement described above.
ip_restrictions:
  restrictions:
  - >-
    The chorus-ai GitHub organization's software is released under the MIT License, with individual
    repositories also listing Apache-2.0; dataset access is separately governed by a licensing
    agreement that participants must sign before gaining access.
distribution_formats:
  - format: DICOM
    notes: Imaging drawn from PACS, under controlled access.
  - format: WFDB
    notes: Waveform telemetry from bedside monitors, held in the enclave under controlled access.
  - format: EDF+ and Persyst
    notes: Waveform EEG drawn from the hospital EEG database, under controlled access.
  - format: OMOP Common Data Model
    notes: >-
      Structured EHR content (demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing
      flowsheets, diagnoses) standardized to OMOP and held in the cloud enclave under controlled
      access.
    source_caveats: >-
      The source names OMOP as the data standard for these content types, not a file format, media
      type or packaging for delivery; no delivery format is stated in the bundle.
  - format: OHNLP
    notes: >-
      Clinical notes extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit; note text remains stored locally
      at contributing sites and only tokens are held centrally.
    source_caveats: >-
      The source names OHNLP as the data standard for tokenized notes, not a file format, media type
      or packaging for delivery; no delivery format is stated in the bundle.
distribution_dates:
  - release_dates:
      - >-
        A released dataset was available to approved users as of August 2025, as reported in the
        September 2025 informational webinar; the project website separately describes a Current
        Released Dataset alongside an Anticipated Final Dataset.
third_party_sharing:
  - is_shared: true
    notes: >-
      Data are made available beyond the contributing institutions under controlled access, and are
      being used for training activities and publications. The project also plans a holdout test set
      accessible for external model validation.
maintainers:
  - name: CHoRUS Consortium
    role: academic_institution
    maintainer_details: >-
      More than 60 consortium members across 20 different institutions maintain the dataset and its
      standards.
  - name: Ciera McCrary
    role: academic_institution
    maintainer_details: >-
      Program Manager, MGH; listed as the contact on the CHoRUS project website, with the address
      cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu.
    source_caveats: >-
      The contact address is transcribed exactly as published on the project website, including its
      apparent typographic error in the domain ("mgh.havard.edu").
  - name: chorus-ai GitHub organization
    role: academic_institution
    maintainer_details: >-
      The CHoRUS GitHub organization hosts 28 repositories of software, semantic mappings, SOPs and
      project management overviews; a package status page lists versions, maintainers and other
      metadata about CHoRUS packages, and a web guide for contributors and users is compiled in the
      chorus-developer repository.
updates:
  update_details: >-
    The dataset is growing toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions across
    9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. As of the September 2025 webinar, imaging
    de-identification was in process for a larger cohort and EEG extraction was in process;
    contributing sites provide regular status updates on their extract progress, tracked on the
    Standards and Data Acquisition project boards.
extension_mechanism:
  contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai
  extension_details: >-
    Contributing sites follow the interactive workflow diagram and SOP documents on the Chorus_SOP
    site to create and submit data extracts, and post issues to the Standards or Data Acquisition
    discussion areas. Clinical collaborators contribute to semantic mapping through the
    chorus-mapping repository, which holds documentation, pooled tabular mappings and a clinical
    validation SOP. Software contributors work through the repositories of the chorus-ai
    organization.
existing_uses:
  - examples:
      - >-
        The datasets are being used for training activities and publications.
intended_uses:
  - use_category: Clinical AI/ML model development
    examples:
    - >-
      Building machine-learning and AI-derived models that characterize acute and critical care
      illness, predict complications, and measure treatment response, in order to improve the care
      and outcomes of patients requiring critical care.
  - use_category: External model validation
    examples:
    - >-
      Validating externally developed models against a sequestered holdout dataset, an activity the
      project plans in order to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models.
  - use_category: Education and workforce development
    examples:
    - >-
      Hands-on AI/ML training in the CHoRUS ecosystem, including structured EHR datasets, clinical
      deep learning, ethics of clinical AI, and the OHDSI/OMOP common data model.
    - >-
      The AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program announced Cohort 2 in a September
      2025 informational webinar: up to 30 trainees were to be selected, with notice of award on
      10 November 2025 and the program running from 17 November 2025 to 31 July 2026, and would
      receive hands-on training on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Network, leveraging the
      CHoRUS data and tools to create practical use cases and conduct collaborative research on the
      Bridge2AI Clinical Care Cloud platform.
    usage_notes: >-
      As of the source webinar (9 September 2025), the Cohort 2 application deadline had not passed
      and no trainees had been selected; this is an announced program rather than a use in progress.
other_tasks:
  - task_details: >-
      Beyond model development, the data serve as a teaching corpus: canonical Jupyter notebooks,
      workshops on the OHDSI tool stack and the OHDSI/OMOP common data model, and didactics on
      generative AI and specific use cases are delivered on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care
      Collaborative Cloud.
future_use_impacts:
  - impact_details: >-
      The project anticipates that the dataset will catalyze biomedical research and expertise
      needed to promote patient-focused deployment of AI in acute and critical care, and that the
      holdout set will aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models.
  - impact_details: >-
      Because the data derive from critically ill patients, the project pairs future use with
      privacy safeguards: transformations that limit re-identification, community-facing ethics
      focus groups on what data is appropriate for public sharing, and analysis of the legal and
      regulatory landscape to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of
      health.
external_resources:
  - name: CHoRUS project website
    external_resources:
    - https://chorus4ai.org/
    description: >-
      Public-facing project site with pages on the team, project overview, tools, data acquisition,
      standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset, and learning resources and
      opportunities.
  - name: chorus-ai GitHub organization
    external_resources:
    - https://github.com/chorus-ai
    description: >-
      28 repositories providing software and tooling for clinical data, validated semantic mappings
      to international standards, standard operating protocols for contributing sites, and project
      management overviews. Repositories include chorus-container-apps, privacy_scan_tool,
      chorus_waveform, chorus_waveform_resources, Chorus_SOP, data_acq_SOP, CTP-deid, UF-Geocoding,
      CHoRUSReports, chorus-extract-upload, chorus-apps-internal, cloud_public and CADA.
    restrictions:
    - >-
      Repositories are public; the project code is licensed under the MIT License, with some
      repositories listing Apache-2.0.
  - name: CHoRUS page on the Bridge2AI website
    external_resources:
    - www.bridge2ai.org/chorus
    description: >-
      Listed as the project website in the chorus-ai GitHub README contact section.

    The two roots are arguments so that the exit code — the thing #833 asked
    for, and the thing four tests of the helpers did not reach — can be
    exercised end to end over a tree built for the purpose.
    """
    base_dir = Path(__file__).parent.parent
    schema_dir = schema_dir or base_dir / "src" / "download" / "prompts"
    eval_base = eval_base or base_dir / "data" / "evaluation_llm"

    schemas = {
        "rubric10-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric10_semantic_schema.json"),
        "rubric20-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"),
    }

    eval_files = discover(eval_base)
    if not eval_files:
        print(f"No evaluation files found in {eval_base}")
        return 1

    print(f"Found {len(eval_files)} evaluation file(s) under {eval_base}\n")

    counts = {("live", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
    counts.update({("kept", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")})
    no_schema: Dict[str, int] = {}
    live_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []
    kept_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []

    for eval_file in eval_files:
        where = "kept" if is_kept(eval_file, eval_base) else "live"
        shown = eval_file.relative_to(eval_base)
        try:
            eval_data = load_evaluation(eval_file)
            if not isinstance(eval_data, dict):
                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"❌ {shown}: failed to load: {e}")
            counts[(where, "unreadable")] += 1
            continue

        rubric = eval_data.get("rubric", "unknown")
        if rubric not in schemas:
            # Named and counted, not skipped in silence: the presence-style
            # rubric10/rubric20 outputs have no schema in this repository, and
            # a reader of the summary should see that they were not judged.
            no_schema[str(rubric)] = no_schema.get(str(rubric), 0) + 1
            continue

        status, errors = classify(eval_data, schemas[rubric])
        counts[(where, status)] += 1
        if status == "invalid":
            (kept_invalid if where == "kept" else live_invalid).append((shown, errors))
        elif status == "superseded":
            print(f"🕐 {shown}: superseded shape — {errors[0]}")

    for label, rows in (("live", live_invalid), ("kept as evidence", kept_invalid)):
        for shown, errors in rows:
            print(f"❌ {shown} ({label}):")
            for error in errors:
                print(f"     {error}")

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("SUMMARY (judged against a schema):")
    for where in ("live", "kept"):
        row = {k: counts[(where, k)] for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
        print(f"  {where:5}  valid {row['valid']:4}  superseded {row['superseded']:3}  "
              f"invalid {row['invalid']:3}  unreadable {row['unreadable']:3}")
    if no_schema:
        print("  no schema in this repository, not judged: "
              + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(no_schema.items())))
    print("=" * 60)

    # A superseded record is historical output of a contract that no longer
    # applies, and one kept under an archive marker is evidence of what an
    # older instrument produced: reported, never rewritten to pass. Only a
    # live invalid artifact fails the run.
    return 0 if not live_invalid and not counts[("live", "unreadable")] else 1


def cli(argv: List[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--file", type=Path, action="append", dest="files",
                        help="validate this exact new output strictly; repeat for multiple files")
    parser.add_argument("--rubric", choices=("rubric10-semantic", "rubric20-semantic"),
                        help="require the named outputs to use this rubric")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.rubric and not args.files:
        parser.error("--rubric requires --file")
    return validate_outputs(args.files, args.rubric) if args.files else main()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(cli())
